title: Opening Disability Compensation Past-Due Release: Spouse Months and Amounts
content:
**Clause.** The spouse addition in the opening past-due release of a Disability Compensation award is the spouse addition plus the spouse aid-and-attendance addition when a spouse is recorded on the award and the most recent spouse addition is marked as needing aid and attendance; the spouse addition alone when a spouse is recorded and the most recent spouse addition is not so marked; and nothing when no spouse is recorded.

**Months counted.** A spouse is recorded when the spouse additions on the award exceed its spouse removals. The amount is counted for each of the whole months elapsed from the most recent spouse addition's effective date to the issue date of the most recent monthly payment. Of those months, as many as fall in the months owed at the individual unemployability rate — never more than the spouse months themselves — take the 100 percent tier's amounts (spouse 220.30, aid and attendance 201.41); the remaining spouse months take the award's own tier.

**Worked cases (hypothetical award at Disability Compensation (40% Combined Rating); most recent monthly payment issued 1 April 2026; no month owed at the individual unemployability rate)**

| Records | Spouse months | Spouse amount |
|---|---|---|
| Spouse added effective 5 November 2025, marked as needing aid and attendance | 4 | 88.12 plus 80.56, that is 168.68, for 4 months: 674.72 |
| Same spouse, not so marked | 4 | 88.12 for 4 months: 352.48 |
| Spouse added and later removed | — | Nothing |

**With months at the individual unemployability rate (hypothetical).** If 2 of the months owed were at the individual unemployability rate, the unmarked spouse above would take 220.30 for 2 months and 88.12 for the other 2: 440.60 plus 176.24, that is 616.84.
